This should be fun, let's go back through Kickstarter:

Imperial Crusade Armada: By the time I got it, I forgot I even backed it. Still haven't even played it.

Empires of the Void: Arrive when they said it would, doesn't hit the table that often. I think maybe twice. It's pretty, but not much substance to it.

Bootleggers: Actually one of my favorite games. Get to play as a gangster in the 20's moving hooch. Techincally a reprint, but I still backed it on kickstarter.

War Stories: Took fricken forever to arrive, way past the point of the estimated delivery. It's an awesome war game, I just don't have anyone to play with because it doesn't mesh well with my girlfriend.

Story War: Backed this the same time as War Stories, which was definitely confusing. It's a party storytelling game, not much to it. With the right group it's fun.

Walk the Plank!: The "prequel" to Get Bit! It's a lite game, but I've had issues with it because of people teaming up. Shared victories causes people to pick sides.

Dungeon Roll: This actually was the game that turned me off from Kickstarter for awhile. It didn't arrive late, the components are great, and the little chest it comes in is cool. It's also cool to see a game that I helped Kickstart on the shelves of Barnes and Nobels everywhere. However, the game is mechanically flawed, and is boring on top of that.

Hunter's Guild: Another example of a game where everything about it is fine, except for the gameplay itself.

Coup: Holy shit! I forgot I kickstarted this. Amazing game, can't recommend it enough. Quick bluffing game that plays closer to poker than anything else.

So I haven't had great experience with it. I enjoy some of the games I got, but overall I should have done more research. The good thing is, most games now have Rahdo or someone else give a run through of it before it comes out, so you can see the game played before backing it. My advice is to not back any game where you can't read the rules. If they don't have a good rule book, the game will never be good.

To add to this, I have backed 2 games recently, and 1 that my girlfriend has backed.

Cuisine a la Card: Me and my girlfriend love deck building games, and this one looks right up our alley since it focuses on two player games.

Periorbis: Resource moving game about being space miners. Looks awesome, good run through by Rahdo. I actually paid extra to get my girlfriend in the game as one of the characters.
